caption: The drawing depicts two wooden doors, both positioned vertically and parallel to each other against a light beige background. The door on the left is a full, arched-top wooden door composed of three vertical planks with visible wood grain and natural textures. Each plank features irregular, wavy vertical lines in reddish-brown tones, as well as smaller, dark circular spots suggestive of nails or fasteners. There is a large circular hole near the bottom of the center plank and a worn, brownish area on the left edge, possibly where a lock or latch would be. The door sits on a row of rectangular, reddish-orange bricks. The object on the right side of the drawing appears to be a shorter, broken section of a similar wooden door or gate, also made up of three planks aligned vertically, with the same wavy reddish lines and small circular nail heads. This object has an irregular, jagged upper edge and also features a round hole near the bottom center, aligned with the planks. It rests on a section of reddish-orange brick similar to the one beneath the full door. Both objects utilize muted browns, reddish tones, and hints of greenish and grayish hues to represent the wood’s aged and weathered appearance. On the bottom right corner of the drawing, there is a handwritten signature and date in a reddish-brown color: "R.W.E. Taylor - 1936."
title: Restoration Drawing: Wall Decoration over Doorway, Facade of Mission House
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
